phases.name: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
phases.description: Turn the catalog brief into explicit workload assumptions, a measurable response budget, and the first query-path boundaries.

phases.name: Build the interactive query path
phases.description: Normalize multilingual queries, serve suggestions, scatter across the inverted index, and rank a bounded first page.

phases.name: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
phases.description: Schedule canonical URLs through a host-aware frontier, enforce crawl policy, and capture durable page snapshots and change events.

phases.name: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
phases.description: Extract text and media signals asynchronously, maintain link-graph features, and publish idempotent index generations.

phases.name: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
phases.description: Observe query and crawl SLOs, scale from measured queues and hot shards, and degrade honestly under partial failure.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Separate the stated brief from working assumptions
steps.content: The live brief requires crawling and indexing billions of pages, relevant low-latency results, billions of daily queries, text/image/video content, autocomplete, relevance ranking, typo/synonym handling, regular index updates, multi-term queries, and multiple languages. For capacity examples only, assume 2B active canonical pages and 2B queries/day: about 23K average QPS and 231K at a 10x peak. These are sizing assumptions, not user-provided forecasts. Treat the 200ms target as p95 from a supported-region edge request to the first result page; separately measure browser submit-to-render and global last-mile latency because geography is unspecified. Set routine fetched-page-to-searchable freshness to p95 <=15 minutes as an initial measurable interpretation of regularly updated; revisit both assumptions with product owners.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Choose a user-visible first-page contract
steps.content: Search should return useful top results quickly without waiting for every shard, media extractor, or crawl job. Keep pagination cursor-based and bind it to the query and index generation so later pages do not silently mix snapshots.

decision.question: What is the latency boundary for the 200ms requirement?
decision.chosen: Measure p95 from edge ingress through receipt of the first ranked page in supported regions; report browser paint and global RTT as separate SLIs.
decision.chosenReason: This makes the service budget actionable while exposing the brief's missing geography and client-render boundary instead of implying every internet path has a fixed RTT.

alternatives.option: Promise 200ms for every global browser paint
alternatives.tradeoff: Not enforceable without explicit user geography, network conditions, and a product-defined measurement boundary.
Hides parsing, merge, ranking, serialization, and gateway time that users experience.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Add search clients
steps.content: Start with web and mobile clients that submit a query, request suggestions while typing, and render a bounded first page with a continuation cursor.

component.label: Web & Mobile Search Clients
component.description: Query entry, autocomplete, ranked result pages, and cursor navigation

properties.purpose: Submit normalized query text and locale, request autocomplete suggestions, render the first ranked result page quickly, and continue with an index-generation-bound cursor. Do not fetch full media into the search response.

component.highlightReason: The user-facing result and latency contract begins at query submission, while image and video media load independently of result metadata.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Add the search edge
steps.content: Terminate TLS, authenticate and rate-limit requests, validate query size and locale, and route traffic to the query path. Keep crawl and administrative workloads off this interactive route.

component.label: Search API Gateway
component.description: TLS, quotas, query validation, and regional routing

properties.purpose: Terminate TLS, enforce query and request-size limits, apply per-client quotas and abuse controls, propagate request deadlines and locale, and route interactive search separately from crawler administration.

component.highlightReason: Search traffic is latency-sensitive and must not be starved by bulk crawling or indexing.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Add a generation-aware popular-query cache
steps.content: Cache only safe, reusable first-page results. A key must include normalized query, language/locale, filters, safe-search mode if enabled, and index generation; short TTLs and generation changes bound staleness.

component.label: Popular Query Cache
component.description: Short-lived first-page results and hot query fragments

properties.purpose: Cache a bounded first page using normalized query, locale, filters, and index generation in the key. Use short TTLs, request coalescing for hot keys, and explicit invalidation on generation changes; never cache user-specific state under a shared key.

component.highlightReason: A small hot set can reduce repeated shard fan-out, but cache keys and invalidation must preserve language, filter, and freshness semantics.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Send user queries to the edge
steps.content: The client sends query text, locale, filters, and a deadline; do not place raw page bodies or large media in this request.

connection.label: Query / autocomplete request
connection.description: Submit a bounded query with locale, filters, request ID, and deadline.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Check the hot-query cache first
steps.content: Use the normalized request identity at the edge. A hit returns a first page from the same index generation; a miss continues to query planning.

connection.label: Generation-aware result lookup
connection.description: Read an eligible cached first page without bypassing locale, filter, or freshness keys.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Add the query coordinator
steps.content: The coordinator owns parsing, deadline propagation, bounded fan-out, top-k merge, and response assembly. It does not crawl pages or synchronously rebuild indexes.

component.label: Search Query Coordinator
component.description: Parse, plan, fan out, merge, and assemble a bounded first page

properties.purpose: Build a typed query plan, enforce expansion and fan-out limits, propagate an absolute deadline, merge shard top-k results, apply the ranker, and return a generation-bound cursor. Keep crawl and index-build work asynchronous.

component.highlightReason: This is the latency-budget owner for multi-term queries and partial-shard behavior.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Route cache misses to query planning
steps.content: The cache miss path passes a normalized request and remaining deadline to the coordinator; it does not wait for a crawl or batch ranking job.

connection.label: Cache miss / query request
connection.description: Forward validated query semantics and the remaining edge deadline.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Return eligible cache hits
steps.content: Cache hits still return explicit generation and freshness metadata so the client and telemetry can distinguish a cached result from a fresh shard read.

connection.label: Cached page + generation
connection.description: Return a valid first page and its index-generation metadata to the gateway.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Size query capacity from the stated scale
steps.content: At the illustrative 2B queries/day baseline, average load is 2,000,000,000 / 86,400 ~= 23,148 QPS. A 10x peak assumption is about 231K QPS. Capacity-test the uncached path at peak rather than assuming cache hit rate; measure the actual query distribution, hot terms, shard skew, and cost per successful query before locking node counts.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Budget the first page end to end
steps.content: Use an initial p95 allocation such as 20ms for edge validation/routing, 20ms for parse and language analysis, 90ms for parallel shard retrieval, 35ms for merge and ranking, and 35ms for serialization/edge return: 200ms total. These are budgets to load-test, not measured facts. Pass one deadline through every hop, reserve margin for tail variance, and stop optional typo/synonym expansion before it consumes the result budget.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Keep the interactive path independent of the crawl path
steps.content: A query must use the last complete searchable generation while crawling, extraction, PageRank, and index compaction continue in the background.

decision.question: Should a query wait for newly crawled pages to finish indexing?
decision.chosen: No. Publish indexed deltas asynchronously and serve the last complete generation with an explicit freshness watermark.
decision.chosenReason: This protects the 200ms search path and makes indexing lag observable instead of coupling query availability to crawler health.

alternatives.option: Synchronously fetch or parse a page on a cache miss
alternatives.tradeoff: Unbounded network and document-processing time breaks predictable query latency and creates a crawler-to-query failure path.

alternatives.option: Wait for a full reindex before serving
alternatives.tradeoff: A full-corpus rebuild can take far longer than the freshness target and risks prolonged stale or unavailable results.

steps.phase: Define search traffic, freshness, and response contracts
steps.title: Set explicit overload behavior
steps.content: Protect the query budget under a burst by shedding optional work before core retrieval.

scaleTrigger.metric: p95 edge-to-first-page latency, uncached QPS, queueing time, and per-shard CPU versus load-test SLO
scaleTrigger.action: Scale query coordinators and search replicas from measured peak demand; cap expansions and cancel straggling shard calls at the shared deadline.
scaleTrigger.impact: Preserves the first useful result and avoids a retry storm or unbounded work when the index is saturated.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Add language-aware query analysis
steps.content: Normalize Unicode and punctuation, detect or accept an explicit locale, tokenize with a versioned language analyzer, and preserve the original terms for exact fallback. Analysis must be bounded and reproducible for a given analyzer version.

component.label: Language & Query Analyzer
component.description: Locale detection, tokenization, normalization, and bounded expansion

properties.purpose: Normalize Unicode, select versioned locale-specific tokenizers and stemming rules, preserve exact original terms, and produce bounded phrase, synonym, and typo candidates with analyzer-version metadata.

component.highlightReason: Language support and multi-term parsing belong in a deterministic, versioned query-analysis stage rather than scattered into every index shard.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Normalize each query once
steps.content: The coordinator sends one bounded query plan to analysis and carries the analyzer version with the request for consistent index interpretation.

connection.label: Query + locale + deadline
connection.description: Normalize the query using a versioned locale analyzer within the remaining budget.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Add a dedicated autocomplete index
steps.content: Keep prefix lookup separate from full result ranking so keystroke suggestions can return a small bounded list without scanning the full web index.

component.label: Prefix & Suggestion Index
component.description: Locale-aware popular completions and query prefixes

properties.purpose: Serve a small locale-aware suggestion set from prefix and popularity structures; update asynchronously from safe aggregate query signals and versioned dictionary data. Apply minimum privacy thresholds before promoting rare queries. Choose partition count and replica topology from measured suggestion volume, query distribution, availability targets, and load tests; the brief does not prescribe counts.

component.highlightReason: Autocomplete is a separate latency and result-size contract from retrieving and ranking documents.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Request suggestions while the user types
steps.content: Use a short prefix request, debounce at the client, and cap the number of completions so the suggestion lane remains cheap.

connection.label: Locale + bounded prefix
connection.description: Look up completions without scanning full document postings.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Return suggestions to the coordinator
steps.content: The query coordinator combines a small suggestion list with the active interaction; suggestions are not treated as ranked search results.

connection.label: Bounded completions
connection.description: Return locale-matched prefix candidates for the client response.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Keep autocomplete bounded and language-specific
steps.content: Suggestions need a per-keystroke budget, locale-aware prefixes, and protection against leaking sensitive rare queries.

decision.question: How should autocomplete share the full-text index?
decision.chosen: Maintain a compact prefix/suggestion structure with its own freshness and privacy thresholds.
decision.chosenReason: Prefix lookup has different data shape, top-N, and privacy needs from full-document retrieval; the full index remains authoritative for submitted searches.

alternatives.option: Run a full ranked document search on every keystroke
alternatives.tradeoff: Wastes shard capacity and increases typing latency for a response that needs only a few candidates.
Rare or sensitive strings can be exposed and low-quality query noise becomes visible.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Add the distributed inverted index
steps.content: Store analyzed terms, positional postings, document fields, content-type metadata, language, freshness, and index generation in a replicated shard cluster.

component.label: Distributed Inverted Search Index
component.description: Term postings, phrase positions, fields, and content signals

properties.purpose: Serve versioned inverted-index postings for analyzed text and media-derived text, including positions for phrase matching, language and content-type fields, freshness timestamps, and document generation. Partition and replicate shards across failure domains. Set shard/partition count and replica topology from measured corpus size, update rate, query fan-out, failure-domain goals, and load-test results; the brief does not prescribe counts.

component.highlightReason: An inverted index and shard-level top-k retrieval provide the core path for billions of pages and multi-term queries.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Turn analysis into a shard query plan
steps.content: The analyzer emits tokens, phrase positions, language, and a bounded expansion set. The coordinator carries the absolute deadline into parallel shard requests.

connection.label: Term / phrase shard plan
connection.description: Retrieve bounded top-k candidates using locale-aware postings and the active generation.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Add top-k merge and relevance ranking
steps.content: Combine lexical relevance with field weights, link authority, freshness, and content-type signals. Keep the scorer bounded and log feature/model versions for quality analysis.

component.label: Top-K Merge & Ranker
component.description: Merge shard candidates and score a bounded result page

properties.purpose: Merge shard-local top-k candidates, score BM25/field matches with versioned authority, freshness, and content-type features, deduplicate canonical URLs, and return a bounded ranked page before the shared deadline.

component.highlightReason: A search engine must rank across shards without scanning every document or performing expensive synchronous graph computation.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Retrieve shard candidates in parallel
steps.content: Each index shard returns a bounded local top-k with document and feature versions; the ranker merges candidates instead of transferring entire posting lists.

connection.label: Shard-local top-k + signals
connection.description: Return bounded candidate sets for global merge and relevance scoring.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Use the ranker for the first page
steps.content: The ranker receives compact authority and freshness snapshots rather than recalculating PageRank for each query.

connection.label: Ranked page + continuation
connection.description: Return the first page, result-quality metadata, and generation-bound cursor.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Assemble the response at the coordinator
steps.content: The coordinator attaches query interpretation, index generation, result freshness, and any partial-shard status before returning to the edge.

connection.label: Ranked response + cursor
connection.description: Return a bounded first page with generation and completeness metadata.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Render the first result page
steps.content: The gateway returns the first page promptly. Full images or video are fetched separately from the result metadata so media transfer does not block search completion.

connection.label: First page / suggestions
connection.description: Deliver ranked snippets, safe media references, and a continuation cursor.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Choose bounded multi-term semantics
steps.content: Support quoted phrases and explicit Boolean operators while preventing pathological expansion from consuming the entire latency budget.

decision.question: How do multiple terms and phrases map to postings?
decision.chosen: Parse a typed query tree, intersect/selective term sets first, use positional postings for phrases, and cap Boolean depth and candidate counts.
decision.chosenReason: The planner can preserve expected multi-term semantics while applying predictable limits before distributed fan-out.

alternatives.option: Treat every query as an unbounded OR over all terms
alternatives.tradeoff: Broad queries return noisy results and can fan out across the entire index.

alternatives.option: Scan full documents after retrieving every term match
alternatives.tradeoff: Moves expensive work onto the latency-critical path and does not scale to billions of pages.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Correct typos without multiplying work without bound
steps.content: Preserve exact terms first. If exact retrieval is weak, add a small, language-aware edit-distance candidate set and curated synonyms; prioritize rare informative terms, cap expansions per query, and stop optional candidates when the deadline is near. Record correction and synonym versions so result quality can be evaluated by language.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Keep query intent and language explicit
steps.content: Support explicit locale hints and confidence-scored detection. When confidence is low, avoid destructive stemming, preserve exact spelling, and prefer language-neutral matching. Version analyzers, dictionaries, and synonyms; deploy them beside the index generation they were built for so a query is not tokenized under incompatible rules.

steps.phase: Build the interactive query path
steps.title: Control shard fan-out and tail latency
steps.content: A slow shard should not hold the first page hostage, but an incomplete result must be identified rather than silently called complete.

scaleTrigger.metric: Per-shard p95/p99 service time, timeout rate, query-to-shard fan-out, and partial-result rate
scaleTrigger.action: Route hot term ranges across replicas, cap shard and expansion fan-out, return a marked partial page only when the deadline expires, and repair or retry stragglers off the user path.
scaleTrigger.impact: Keeps common multi-term queries within the response budget while making coverage loss measurable.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Add crawl scheduling
steps.content: Prioritize discovery from sitemaps, changed-page signals, known links, and recrawl history. The scheduler assigns eligible URLs but workers enforce the final per-host lease and policy before fetch.

component.label: Crawl Scheduler
component.description: Prioritize discovery, recrawl windows, and host-safe work

properties.purpose: Prioritize sitemap and link discovery, recrawl pages by observed change/freshness class, honor source policy, and enqueue canonical URL candidates with host partition and deadline metadata. Keep crawl scheduling separate from interactive query capacity.

component.highlightReason: Billions of pages require continuous distributed discovery and recrawl rather than a one-time batch.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Add a host-sharded crawl frontier
steps.content: Partition frontier work by normalized host so a worker can enforce politeness and a delayed host does not block unrelated domains.

component.label: Host-Sharded URL Frontier
component.description: Durable scheduled URLs, host delays, and retry state

properties.purpose: Persist canonical URL work, shard by normalized host, schedule next-eligible times, and carry attempt count, source, priority, and crawl-policy version. Apply backpressure when workers or downstream extraction are saturated.

component.highlightReason: Host-aware scheduling prevents a crawl spike from becoming abusive or allowing one slow domain to block the whole corpus.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Schedule crawl work durably
steps.content: The scheduler writes eligible canonical URL tasks to the frontier; retries retain host affinity and do not bypass the next-allowed-fetch time.

connection.label: Prioritized URL tasks
connection.description: Enqueue host-partitioned crawl tasks with due time and policy metadata.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Add horizontally scaled crawler workers
steps.content: Workers lease one eligible URL, fetch with bounded redirects/timeouts, and emit a result only after the fetch outcome is recorded.

component.label: Polite Crawler Fleet
component.description: Rate-limited fetches, redirect handling, and link discovery

properties.purpose: Lease due URLs by host, enforce per-host concurrency and delay, recheck robots policy, bound redirects/body size/time, reject private or unsafe network destinations, and emit versioned fetch outcomes and discovered links.

component.highlightReason: Distributed workers scale throughput, while host-scoped gates, SSRF defenses, and resource limits protect both source sites and the crawler.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Lease only due URLs
steps.content: Workers consume the frontier only when host policy and next-fetch time permit; they release or reschedule a lease on timeout or backpressure.

connection.label: Due URL lease
connection.description: Deliver bounded fetch work only after host eligibility checks.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Add a canonical URL and host registry
steps.content: Track canonical URL identity, redirect aliases, content fingerprints, robots policy version, host delay, lease, last-fetch result, and recrawl due time.

component.label: URL & Host Registry
component.description: Canonical identities, dedupe state, leases, and policy metadata

properties.purpose: Store canonical URL and redirect mappings, exact/content fingerprints, host politeness tokens, robots policy version, lease state, fetch status, and next recrawl time. Use conditional lease/version updates so concurrent workers do not fetch the same URL without authorization.

component.highlightReason: Canonicalization and host state prevent duplicate fetches, duplicate index documents, and violations of crawl politeness.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Validate and deduplicate before fetching
steps.content: The registry decides whether a URL is canonical, already in flight, recently fetched, or blocked by host policy.

connection.label: Canonicalize / acquire host lease
connection.description: Resolve aliases, deduplicate, and atomically check fetch eligibility.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Return an eligible fetch lease
steps.content: Only a current lease authorizes a fetch. If policy changes or a lease expires, workers must stop or reacquire before processing the response.

connection.label: Fetch lease + policy version
connection.description: Return a fenced lease and the current host policy required for safe fetch.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Make crawl politeness and safety explicit
steps.content: Every URL is untrusted input. Resolve and revalidate destination addresses after redirects, block private/link-local ranges, bound response bytes and decompression, and do not let robots-policy fetches or DNS failures bypass host backoff.

decision.question: How should robots rules and per-host rate limits be enforced?
decision.chosen: Maintain versioned robots policy with expiry, acquire a host token/lease immediately before fetch, and apply bounded exponential backoff on 429, 5xx, DNS, and timeout outcomes.
decision.chosenReason: The worker needs an atomic last-mile gate because queued policy can become stale while waiting; failure backoff protects the origin and fleet.

alternatives.option: Apply only a global worker rate
alternatives.tradeoff: A global limit still allows a single host to receive a harmful burst.

alternatives.option: Check robots only at discovery time
alternatives.tradeoff: Policy can change between enqueue and fetch, and redirects can leave the checked host.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Add a versioned raw-page archive
steps.content: Keep fetched snapshots outside the query serving path. Apply retention by crawl class and store checksums and source metadata for reprocessing.

component.label: Raw Page & Snapshot Archive
component.description: Versioned compressed fetch snapshots and checksums

properties.purpose: Store bounded, compressed, checksummed page snapshots and response metadata under canonical URL/version keys. Apply retention and lifecycle policies by source and recrawl class; do not retain unbounded duplicate bodies.

component.highlightReason: Durable snapshots allow extraction and indexing to retry without refetching every origin.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Archive a successful fetch
steps.content: Store the snapshot and checksum before publishing the fetch-completed event so downstream workers can retry from durable input.

connection.label: Bounded page snapshot
connection.description: Persist a versioned snapshot and checksum for safe reprocessing.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Add a crawl change stream
steps.content: Publish committed fetch outcomes and discovered-link batches after the registry and snapshot are durable. Consumers can then process each URL version idempotently.

component.label: Crawl Change Event Stream
component.description: Durable fetch outcomes, content changes, and link discoveries

properties.purpose: Publish versioned fetch-completed, content-changed, redirect, and discovered-link events after durable state is recorded. Partition by canonical URL for ordered updates and retain enough history for bounded consumer recovery.

component.highlightReason: An event boundary decouples irregular web fetching from extraction, link analysis, and index updates.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Publish committed crawl results
steps.content: Events carry canonical URL, content hash, snapshot pointer, fetch time, policy version, and a monotonic document version; avoid embedding full page bodies in the broker.

connection.label: Versioned fetch / link event
connection.description: Signal durable snapshots and canonical changes to independent consumers.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Add a bounded retry and dead-letter queue
steps.content: Separate retryable origin failures from poison documents or repeated policy errors. Preserve the URL version, reason, attempt count, and next retry time for operator review.

component.label: Crawl Retry & Dead-Letter Queue
component.description: Bounded retry state and inspectable terminal failures

properties.purpose: Retain retryable fetch and extraction failures with canonical URL, version, class, attempts, and due time. Quarantine poison inputs and policy failures for inspection; cap retries and require safe replay eligibility.

component.highlightReason: A poison URL must not block a host partition or loop forever, and transient failures need a bounded recovery path.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Quarantine exhausted crawl events
steps.content: Route terminal or exhausted work to an inspectable queue; preserve normal broker consumers and query serving while operators investigate.

connection.label: Exhausted / poison work
connection.description: Quarantine failed work with a reason and replay eligibility.

steps.phase: Discover pages with polite distributed crawling
steps.title: Replay only after policy and version checks
steps.content: A retry re-enters the host-aware frontier after backoff and a fresh robots/lease check; it never replays a stale authorization or overwrites a newer URL version.

connection.label: Reviewed, backoff-eligible replay
connection.description: Requeue safe work through the same host and version gates as new tasks.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Add asynchronous content extraction
steps.content: Extract safe text and metadata from HTML; derive image text from alt text/OCR and video text from captions/transcripts where available. Keep extraction budgets, parsers, and provenance per media type.

component.label: Text, Image & Video Extractors
component.description: HTML parsing, OCR/caption metadata, and transcript extraction

properties.purpose: Read bounded archived snapshots, extract sanitized text, titles, links, image alt/OCR signals, and available video captions/transcripts, and attach source offsets, media type, language, extraction version, and checksum. Quarantine malformed or oversized content.

component.highlightReason: Multimodal support belongs in asynchronous extraction so large media parsing does not delay a search query.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Process committed fetch events
steps.content: The extractor resolves the archive pointer and processes each canonical URL version once; duplicate deliveries are safe to retry.

connection.label: Snapshot pointer + document version
connection.description: Trigger versioned extraction from durable archived content.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Add page and link metadata storage
steps.content: Keep canonical document metadata, extracted fields, language, links, fingerprints, crawl time, and tombstone/version state addressable independently of raw snapshots.

component.label: Page & Link Metadata Store
component.description: Canonical document state, extracted fields, links, and versions

properties.purpose: Persist canonical URL, title/snippet fields, language, content type, link edges, fingerprints, crawl/extraction versions, freshness, and deletion tombstones. Support idempotent version checks and bulk graph reads for offline rank computation.

component.highlightReason: The search index is a derived serving structure; canonical metadata and version/tombstone state are needed for rebuilds and safe updates.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Commit extracted content and link edges
steps.content: Write extracted metadata idempotently by canonical URL and document version. Keep source offsets and extraction provenance for snippets and quality audits.

connection.label: Versioned fields + link graph
connection.description: Persist extracted fields, provenance, links, and tombstone state.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Index media signals without serving media inline
steps.content: The brief asks for text, images, and videos. Search can discover media through metadata, captions, transcript, OCR, and safe content references without forcing full binary payloads into the index or result request.

decision.question: What does supporting image and video content mean in this design?
decision.chosen: Index text and metadata plus available alt/OCR, captions, and transcripts with content-type and source provenance; keep original media in bounded external references.
decision.chosenReason: This makes image/video pages searchable while controlling fetch, extraction, storage, and first-page latency. Unsupported or unavailable derived signals remain explicitly absent.

alternatives.option: Download and embed every full image and video in the search index
alternatives.tradeoff: Creates unbounded storage and extraction work and makes query serving depend on media transfer.
Fails the stated requirement to support different content types.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Add an idempotent index builder
steps.content: Consume extracted document versions, write incremental segments, and periodically compact/rebuild offline. A candidate generation is validated before it becomes query-visible.

component.label: Index Builder & Publisher
component.description: Idempotent deltas, compaction, and generation publication

properties.purpose: Build idempotent per-document index deltas from extracted versions, apply tombstones, compact segments, validate analyzer/schema compatibility, and publish an immutable generation only after completeness and integrity checks pass.

component.highlightReason: Separating index construction from serving lets the query path use one complete generation while updates and compaction proceed.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Send versioned deltas to the builder
steps.content: The builder consumes extracted fields and provenance, rejecting stale document versions and making retries idempotent.

connection.label: Extracted document delta
connection.description: Build a searchable update from a specific canonical URL version.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Compute link authority outside the query path
steps.content: Run PageRank or a similar graph computation from versioned link edges in batch or incremental windows. Publish bounded feature snapshots; do not run graph traversal per user query.

component.label: Link Authority & Freshness Jobs
component.description: Offline PageRank-like scores and freshness feature snapshots

properties.purpose: Compute versioned link-authority and freshness features from committed graph metadata in bounded batch/incremental jobs. Publish snapshots with generation, timestamp, and quality checks; never traverse the full graph synchronously during a query.

component.highlightReason: PageRank improves relevance at web scale only when its expensive graph work is decoupled from interactive search.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Build authority features from committed graph state
steps.content: The graph job reads committed metadata and link versions, so it does not score uncommitted or partially extracted page relationships.

connection.label: Versioned pages + link edges
connection.description: Compute offline authority and freshness features from committed graph state.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Supply ranking features from a bounded snapshot
steps.content: The ranker reads a versioned feature snapshot or compact feature fields with the candidate set; stale features are measured and never block all results.

connection.label: Authority / freshness snapshot
connection.description: Provide versioned ranking features without a synchronous graph traversal.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Publish the active search generation
steps.content: After a delta or rebuilt segment passes validation, the builder atomically exposes it to the index cluster and records the resulting generation and watermark.

connection.label: Validated index generation
connection.description: Publish searchable segments only after integrity and analyzer-version checks.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Swap generations atomically
steps.content: Queries and cursors must not mix partially written segments or incompatible analyzers.

decision.question: How should a rebuild become visible?
decision.chosen: Build an immutable candidate generation, validate document counts/checksums/analyzer versions, then atomically switch the serving alias; retain the previous generation for rollback.
decision.chosenReason: Readers see either a complete old generation or a complete new one, while operators can revert without reconstructing serving state.

alternatives.option: Update live shards in place during a large rebuild
alternatives.tradeoff: Readers can observe mixed generations, and a bad batch is difficult to roll back atomically.
A corrupt or incomplete rebuild can remove valid search coverage.

steps.phase: Extract, rank, and publish searchable content
steps.title: Make regular freshness measurable
steps.content: Record fetch time, extraction completion, indexing completion, and active-generation time per canonical URL. The initial p95 <=15 minute target applies to eligible changed pages after successful fetch; pages that fail policy or origin access are reported separately, not falsely counted as fresh. Full recrawl duration, update lag, and percentage of eligible pages within target are separate measurements.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Add search and crawl telemetry
steps.content: Correlate each query and document version across gateway, shards, crawling, extraction, and index publication without logging sensitive query contents by default.

component.label: Search Quality & Freshness Telemetry
component.description: Latency, relevance, shard health, crawl/index lag, and cost

properties.purpose: Track p50/p95/p99 first-page latency, shard timeouts and skew, partial-result rate, zero-result/reformulation signals, language coverage, crawl politeness, retry/DLQ age, extraction/index lag, generation integrity, and cost per successful query. Minimize raw query retention.

component.highlightReason: A numeric latency objective and regular-refresh promise need end-to-end metrics and quality/freshness signals, not infrastructure health alone.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Measure edge and query quality
steps.content: Correlate request IDs and deadline budgets across the interactive path; sample or aggregate query text under a documented privacy policy.

connection.label: Edge latency / quota signals
connection.description: Measure ingress-to-first-page latency, throttling, and request outcomes.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Watch search-index health
steps.content: Alert on replica loss, hot-term shard skew, generation inconsistency, and partial results before the first-page objective is repeatedly missed.

connection.label: Shard / replica / generation health
connection.description: Expose query latency, replica health, skew, and active generation.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Watch crawler safety and freshness
steps.content: Track fetch outcomes, per-host delay compliance, redirect loops, blocked destinations, and eligible-page freshness without rewarding a high fetch count that violates policy.

connection.label: Fetch / policy / host signals
connection.description: Measure crawl coverage and policy compliance by host and result class.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Watch event lag and terminal failures
steps.content: Alert on consumer lag, retry age, poison-page clusters, and dead-letter growth; give operators a safe replay path with URL/version fencing.

connection.label: Event lag / retry volume
connection.description: Observe broker health and the time from successful fetch to extraction.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Watch index publication
steps.content: Measure extracted-to-searchable lag, stale-version rejection, compaction duration, and generation rollback so regular updates are observable.

connection.label: Index lag / generation checks
connection.description: Track update freshness, integrity validation, and publication/rollback.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Watch frontier saturation
steps.content: The frontier exposes due-work age and host-level backpressure so increasing crawler concurrency cannot silently bypass politeness.

connection.label: Due age / host backpressure
connection.description: Scale workers only when due work, downstream capacity, and host policy permit.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Degrade visibly when shards fail
steps.content: If a shard misses the shared deadline, return the best bounded page only with explicit completeness metadata and telemetry; do not present a partial result as a complete index answer.

decision.question: What should happen when one or more shards time out?
decision.chosen: Use healthy replicas or bounded hedged reads within the same deadline; if coverage remains incomplete, return a marked partial page or retryable error according to product policy.
decision.chosenReason: The system protects first-page latency without hiding the loss of search coverage or amplifying the outage with uncontrolled retries.

alternatives.tradeoff: Violates the response target and lets one hot shard stall every query.

alternatives.option: Return partial results without telling the client
alternatives.tradeoff: Misrepresents relevance and can undermine trust in the search product.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Scale query capacity from measured demand
steps.content: Use load tests that include hot terms, broad multi-term queries, locale mix, cold cache, and replica loss; average QPS alone misses the tail-risk cases.

scaleTrigger.metric: p95/p99 first-page latency, uncached peak QPS, shard CPU/queue depth, replica availability, and result completeness
scaleTrigger.action: Add query coordinators and rebalance/replicate hot shards before the p95 budget is consumed; keep crawler/index workers in separately bounded pools.
scaleTrigger.impact: Maintains search responsiveness at the assumed peak without letting background ingestion contend for interactive resources.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Scale indexing from freshness lag
steps.content: Add workers only when extraction, storage, and index-shard capacity can accept the added throughput; otherwise use backpressure and prioritize changed/important pages.

scaleTrigger.metric: Eligible-page fetched-to-searchable p95, frontier due age, broker lag, DLQ age, and index compaction headroom
scaleTrigger.action: Scale extraction and index building independently, prioritize by freshness class, and pause low-priority recrawls before violating host limits or query capacity.
scaleTrigger.impact: Improves freshness without converting a crawler burst into an index outage or origin traffic spike.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: Review relevance and coverage, not only speed
steps.content: Track judged query sets by language and content type, zero-result rate, click/reformulation signals, duplicate canonical results, stale-page exposure, and ranking regressions. Roll analyzer, synonym, and ranking versions back independently. Use aggregate feedback carefully: clicks are biased and are not ground truth by themselves.

steps.phase: Operate freshness, quality, and failure recovery
steps.title: End-to-end design check
steps.content: The interactive path is client -> gateway -> cache/query coordinator -> locale analysis and suggestions -> distributed inverted-index shards -> bounded top-k merge/ranking -> first page. The independent ingestion path is scheduler -> host-sharded frontier -> polite crawler -> canonical registry and snapshot archive -> versioned event stream -> text/image/video extraction -> page/link metadata, authority features, and idempotent index generation. Confirm the 200ms boundary and 15-minute freshness assumption with stakeholders, then validate both against load and relevance tests; neither is a measured production guarantee yet.
